expectations.text: Module has a docstring with a one-line summary of what the module provides
expectations.evidence: First line: "A thread-safe token-bucket rate limiter."

expectations.text: TokenBucket class docstring includes an Attributes: section documenting public attributes
expectations.evidence: Class docstring lines 46-50: "Attributes:" documenting rate ("Sustained refill rate, in tokens per second. Read-only.") and capacity.

expectations.text: acquire and try_acquire have docstrings with Args: and Returns: sections; Raises: present where the code raises for invalid input
expectations.evidence: Both have Args:, Returns:, Raises:; acquire's Raises even covers the negative-timeout ValueError raised at line 135.

expectations.text: All docstrings use triple double quotes with descriptive (not imperative) first lines ending in a period
expectations.evidence: All 9 docstrings use """; first lines are descriptive and period-terminated, e.g. "Initializes a full bucket.", "Attempts to take `n` tokens without blocking.", "Rejects token counts that are non-positive or can never fit."

expectations.text: With type annotations present, docstrings describe semantics without repeating the types
expectations.evidence: Entries give behavior, not types: "n: Number of tokens to take. May be fractional. Must be positive..."; "timeout: Maximum seconds to wait. None (the default) waits indefinitely."

expectations.text: try_acquire's Returns: explains the True/False semantics; acquire documents its blocking behavior
expectations.evidence: try_acquire Returns: "True if the tokens were taken; False if fewer than `n` tokens are currently available."; acquire summary: "Takes `n` tokens, blocking until they are available." plus timeout semantics in Returns.

expectations.text: Any inline comments are separated from code by at least two spaces and explain intent rather than restating code
expectations.evidence: No trailing inline comments; block comments (lines 144-146, 154-155) explain intent, e.g. "Another thread may take the tokens while we sleep, so the loop rechecks availability rather than assuming success."

expectations.text: Thread-safety behavior is stated in the class or module docstring (either safe or not — just stated)
expectations.evidence: Class docstring: "safe for use from multiple threads... All state is guarded by an internal lock; instances may be shared freely across threads."

expectations.text: Module docstring includes a typical usage example block
expectations.evidence: Module docstring lines 10-22: "Typical usage example:" with blocking and non-blocking code samples (bucket.acquire(); if bucket.try_acquire(5): ...).

summary.notes: Full-detail Google-style documentation satisfies every shared assertion and the CC2 usage-example requirement.
